title.purpose: The project's name, hard left in the masthead; truncates, never wraps.

body.purpose: Prose, ledes, notices and status lines at a 62ch measure; the app's input values.

body-sm.purpose: Bylines, asides, consequences, help lines, fact terms, entry notes, the update bar.

label.purpose: Button labels, never wrapping; field labels at the same size and weight with prose leading.

state.purpose: State words, uppercase: PENDING, NOT IN THE REPO, AVAILABLE, APPLIED, IN THE REPO, UP TO DATE, PINNED.

mono.purpose: Machine strings only: versions, hashes, paths, URLs, logins, dates; tabular figures.

motion.name: ease-out
motion.purpose: The one easing: colour changes on hover and press (links, buttons, input borders).

motion.name: dur-short
motion.purpose: The one duration. Focus rings and state changes are instant, never transitioned.

motion.name: success-hold
motion.purpose: A button holds its success label (Copied, Saved) on an ink outline, then its own label returns.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: prefers-reduced-motion drops every colour fade and the press sink.

breakpoints.name: split

breakpoints.name: wide

narrative.overview:
The admin page reads like the backend's own changelog: what is running (a version and the commit it was built from), what is unreleased (drop-in migrations that exist only on this device), and what the app needs (its login, its UI). The example app is a typeset index of the user's records on the same paper. Paper discipline on a dark ground: hairlines, measure, type; no cards, no gradients, no glow. It refuses the centred card of buttons and the stack of cards for form, list and buttons.

The physical scene: the owner, at home in the evening, opens the panel inside Home Assistant's dark theme on a laptop or a phone. The ground is Home Assistant's own neutral dark at chroma 0, so the page sits flush in the panel; the warmth lives in the ink. The density is a document's, not a dashboard's: one left-hung column, each section's state first, then the one action that resolves it, with its consequence written beside it.

Nothing moves. Hover and press change colour over 150ms on one ease-out curve; a pressed button sinks 1px; focus rings and every state change are instant, and reduced motion drops even the colour fades.
keyCharacteristics: Home Assistant's neutral ground (#121212, bars #1a1a1a) under a warm off-white ink in three steps.
Green only to press, amber only for what needs attention, red only for what failed.
One family for Thai and Latin (IBM Plex Sans Thai 400/700); IBM Plex Mono only for machine strings.
Rules, not boxes: 1px between entries, 2px between sections, dotted leaders in the index.
States are words; the only icon is the new-tab arrow.
Silent success; a costly action states its consequence.

rules.name: The One Ink, One Meaning Rule
rules.body: Green means press, amber means needs attention, red means failed, and none stands in for another. A ticked note is meta ink, "Copied" and "Saved" are ink, a selection is umber; amber never fills a button or colours a link.

rules.name: The Host's Ground Rule
rules.body: The ground is Home Assistant's own neutral dark at chroma 0 (#121212 content, #1a1a1a bars), so the page sits flush in its panel; the warmth lives in the ink (hue 85). This deliberately overrides Hallmark's tint-every-neutral gate, and the owner signed off on it. Never a blue-black slate, never pure black, never pure white.

rules.name: The One Family, Two Scripts Rule
rules.body: IBM Plex Sans Thai sets Thai and Latin alike, at 400 and 700 only, roman only. No second sans, no italic, no other weight.

rules.name: The Machine Strings Rule
rules.body: Mono is for what a machine wrote or will read: versions, hashes, paths, URLs, logins, dates, and a field whose value is a release tag or a URL. Never for prose, labels or headings.

rules.name: The Thai Leading Rule
rules.body: Thai stacks marks above and below the line: 1.3 for headings, one-line controls and state words, 1.6 for prose. Never line-height 1.

rules.name: The Left-Hung Column Rule
rules.body: The reading column starts at the gutter under the masthead name and never centres. Its width is the only thing a page tunes (46rem admin, 40rem app).

rules.name: The More-Above Rule
rules.body: A section head has more space above it than below: 3rem, a 2px rule and 2rem above; 0.5rem below.

rules.name: The Paper Rule
rules.body: Surfaces are flat in every state. Depth is one tonal step and a rule; a press is a 1px sink; nothing casts a shadow or glows.

rules.name: The Two-Pixel Rule
rules.body: Every corner in the system is 2px. A pill, a circle or a large radius would be a second shape language.

rules.name: The Consequence Rule
rules.body: A costly action states its consequence beside its button in 0.875rem meta ink ("restarts the add-on", "no restart", "to serve the new source"). A reversible action needs no confirmation.

rules.name: The Silent Success Rule
rules.body: Success is a status line in place, or the button itself turning ink on its outline for 1.5s. Never a toast.

rules.name: The State Word Rule
rules.body: A state is a word, never a badge, dot, glyph or colour chip.

dos: Do keep the token block between `/* tokens:start */` and `/* tokens:end */` identical, line for line, in both pages, and mirror any change in this file's frontmatter; `scripts/local-e2e.sh` fails when the two blocks differ.
Do lay the ground in `paper` (#121212) and bands in `paper-2` (#1a1a1a) at chroma 0, and keep the warmth in the ink (hue 85).

Do give every button all eight states: default, hover, focus-visible (2px ring, 2px out, instant), active (1px sink), disabled (0.55), loading (0.8, a label that says what is happening), error (red outline), success (ink outline for 1.5s).
Do write a costly action's consequence beside its button, in 0.875rem meta ink.
Do keep buttons and inputs 2.75rem (44px) tall with 2px corners.
Do set versions, hashes, paths, URLs, logins and dates in IBM Plex Mono, and break a path only after a `/`.
Do separate entries with a 1px hairline and sections with a 2px rule, with more space above a section head than below it.

Do take colour, the type scale, spacing, radius and motion from tokens (code's 0.875em is the one relative size); keep raw values to component dimensions (column widths, the 11rem QR, the 3.5rem masthead) and optical offsets (the 3px underline, the 2px focus offset).
donts: Don't use green for a state: a done note's checkbox is meta ink, "Copied" and "Saved" are ink, a text selection is umber.
Don't use amber for an action: it never fills a button or colours a link.
Don't tint the ground or swap it for a blue-black slate, pure black, or pure-white text.
Don't add cards, shadows, glows or gradients; structure is rules and type.
Don't confirm a success with a toast.
Don't set italic or any weight but 400 and 700: only those faces ship, so anything else is synthesized.
Don't let a glyph or emoji stand in for an icon or a state; states are words.
Don't let a button label, link text or state word wrap, or a path break inside a name.
Don't set an input's text below 1rem (16px): phones zoom the page when such a field takes focus.
